answer_1.quote: Inspired by these successful applications of generative approaches we here propose applying, for the first time, a generative seq2seq model to the lexical substitution task.

answer_2.quote: We measure the performances on the task with the standard metrics for lexical substitution, i.e., best and oot.

answer_4.quote: We set up a test where an annotator is provided with a target word in context and a set of substitutes that are equally distributed among the gold and the generated ones.
answer_4.guideline: A substitute is wrong if it is an inflection of the target; modifies the meaning; results in a wrong structure; has a different inflected form. A substitute is correct if it is in its base form and not in the same inflection as the target.
